topics.name: Modern pronouns: you, your, yours, I, me
Subject-verb agreement in the simple present

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a correct negative command?
options: Do not crush that little worm.
questions.rule: A negative command is Do not / Don't + base verb: Do not crush.

options: An earthworm live in moist soil.
An earthworm are living in moist soil.
An earthworm lives in moist soil.
questions.rule: A singular subject (an earthworm) takes a verb with -s in the simple present: lives.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct pronoun.
options: This garden is yours, so please look after it.
This garden is your, so please look after it.
This garden is your's, so please look after it.
questions.rule: With no noun after it, use the possessive pronoun yours. It never takes an apostrophe.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct preposition?
options: Farmers depend at earthworms for rich soil.
Farmers depend on earthworms for rich soil.
Farmers depend to earthworms for rich soil.
questions.rule: The verb depend is followed by on: depend on someone.

options: The waste is turned into compost by the worms.
The waste is turn into compost by the worms.
The waste are turned into compost by the worms.
questions.rule: Passive = is/are + past participle. Waste is singular, so: is turned.

options: Each of the bees have a job in the hive.
Each of the bee has a job in the hive.
Each of the bees has a job in the hive.
questions.rule: Each of + plural noun takes a singular verb: Each of the bees has.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: Don't step on the ants, are you?
Don't step on the ants, will you?
Don't step on the ants, do you?
questions.rule: A negative command takes the tag will you?: Don't step on the ants, will you?

options: Neither the spider nor the ants harms the young plants.
Neither the spider nor the ants harm the young plants.
Neither the spider or the ants harm the young plants.
questions.rule: Neither ... nor go together, and the verb agrees with the nearer subject: the ants harm.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Meera is one person, so the simple present verb takes -s: feeds.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A command uses the base form of the verb: please turn ... and let.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Prevent ... from is followed by the -ing form: from eating.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive = was + past participle: the pit was built by the students.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The subject of a verb takes the subject pronoun: Tanvi and I planted (you would say I planted).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: People is plural, so the present perfect uses have: People have started.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive with a modal = modal + be + past participle: should not be thrown.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The verb insist takes on: she insists on feeding the birds.
A negative command begins with Don't + base verb.
No noun follows, so use the possessive pronoun yours, just like mine.

questions.before: The queen bee and her workers
questions.rule: Two subjects joined by and make a plural subject: they live.
We say famous for something.

questions.after: by the eco club every Saturday.
questions.rule: The garden receives the action and by the eco club names the doer, so use the passive: is watered.
Let + object + base verb (no to): Let them enjoy.

questions.before: The bees in this hive work hard; the honey on our table is
questions.rule: At the end, with no noun after it, use the possessive pronoun theirs.

questions.after: the spiders in the corner, Aunt Leela thanked them for catching the mosquitoes.
questions.rule: We complain about something and thank someone for something.
A negative command: Do not + base verb + object.
yours stands alone at the end; not comes after is.
Passive: object first, then was + past participle + by + doer.
Neither of + plural noun takes a singular verb: likes.
grateful to a person or creature, for what they do.

chat: Riya, there is a worm on the path.
options: Oh! Let's not stepping on it.
Oh! Let's not step on it.
Oh! Let us not to step on it.
questions.rule: Let's not + base verb: Let's not step on it.

options: No, it is not mine. It is hers.
No, it is not my. It is hers.
No, it is not mine. It is her's.
questions.rule: Without a noun after them, use mine and hers. hers has no apostrophe.

options: It eat dead leaves and soil.
It eating dead leaves and soil.
It eats dead leaves and soil.
questions.rule: It takes a verb with -s in the simple present: It eats.

options: It was make by our eco club.
It was made by our eco club.
It made by our eco club.
questions.rule: Passive = was + past participle: It was made by our eco club.

options: No, I am not scared from them. I like them.
No, I am not scared of them. I like them.
No, I am not scared at them. I like them.
questions.rule: We say scared of something.

chat: My little brother keeps poking the ants with a stick.
options: Tell to him to leave them alone.
Tell him to leave them alone.
questions.rule: Tell + person + to + verb: Tell him to leave them alone.

chat: Did the bees sting anyone at the picnic?
questions.rule: Nobody is singular, and the past participle of sting is stung: nobody was stung.

options: Arjun and me did, ma'am. The idea was his, but the work was ours.
Arjun and I did, ma'am. The idea was him, but the work was our.
Arjun and I did, ma'am. The idea was his, but the work was ours.
questions.rule: Subject: Arjun and I. With no noun after them, use his and ours.
Add Do not before the base verb: Do not disturb the bees.

options: The soil was loosened by worms.
The soil is loosened by worms.
The soil is loosen by worms.
questions.rule: Simple present passive = is/are + past participle: is loosened. The tense stays present.

questions.prompt: Change the subject to 'Ants' and rewrite the sentence.
questions.source: An ant carries food to its nest.
options: Ants carries food to their nest.
Ants carry food to their nest.
Ants carry food to its nest.
questions.rule: A plural subject takes the base verb (carry) and the plural pronoun their.

options: Riya is fond of watch butterflies.
Riya is fond to watching butterflies.
Riya is fond of watching butterflies.
questions.rule: fond of is followed by a noun or an -ing form: fond of watching.

questions.source: Mother said to me, "Don't crush the ants."
options: Mother told me not to crush the ants.
Mother told me that not to crush the ants.
Mother told me don't crush the ants.
questions.rule: A negative command becomes told + person + not to + verb.

questions.source: Kabir said, "My garden has many earthworms."
options: Kabir said that my garden had many earthworms.
Kabir said that his garden had many earthworms.
Kabir said that his garden have many earthworms.
questions.rule: My changes to his (Kabir's), and has moves back to had.

questions.source: We must not kill harmless creatures.
options: Harmless creatures must not be killed by us.
Harmless creatures must not be kill by us.
Harmless creatures must not killed by us.
questions.rule: Modal passive = modal + be + past participle: must not be killed.

options: By whom were these tulsi plants planted?
By whom was these tulsi plants planted?
By whom were these tulsi plants plant?
questions.rule: Who becomes By whom; plural plants take were + past participle planted.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this note.
questions.rule: Grandpa is one person: keeps. People is plural: visit.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Passive needs the past participle: was dug, was covered. As a subject, say Tanvi and I.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: interest in, for + a period of time (two years), depend on.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this notice.
questions.rule: Commands use the base verb: don't throw, never forget. After let + object, use the base verb: do.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Object of gave: Meera and me. Passive: was planted. Before a noun use her: her favourite flower.
